Jensen, 

I'm not sure what the numbers of your colors mean, but if you change "Red" and "Black" to what you want then it should work. 

Natal_Plot +
theme_bw() +
scale_shape_manual(

value = c("CRBNo"=23, "CWSNo"=24, "LSKNo"=22, "USKNo"=21, "CWSYes"=24,"LSKYes"=22, "USKYes"=21, "LSKYesHatch"=22)
, breaks = c("CRBNo","CWSNo","LSKNo","USKNo","LSKYesHatch")
, name = "Classification"
, labels = c(" Tucannon Grande Ronde Imnaha ", " Clearwater Salmon ", " Lower Snake ", " Upper Snake ", " Hatchery Yearling ")
)+
scale_fill_manual(

breaks = c("CRBNo", "CWSNo", "LSKNo", "USKNo", "LSKYesHatch")
, name = "Classification"
, labels = c(" Tucannon Grande Ronde Imnaha ", " Clearwater Salmon ", " Lower Snake ", " Upper Snake ", " Hatchery Yearling ")

, values=c("CRBNo"="Red", "CWSNo"="Red", "LSKNo"="Red", "USKNo"="Red", "CWSYes"="Black", "LSKYes"="Black","USKYes"="Black", "LSKYesHatch"="Black")
)+

scale_x_discrete(breaks=c("CRB", "CWS", "LSK", "USK"),
labels=c(' Tucannon Grande Ronde Imnaha', ' Clearwater Salmon',
' Lower Snake', ' Upper Snake')) +
opts(panel.background=theme_rect(size=2) ,
axis.text.y=theme_text(size=14, face="bold", hjust=.9),
axis.text.x=theme_text(hjust=.5, vjust=.75, size=12, face="bold"),
panel.background=theme_rect(size=1.5), plot.title=theme_text(hjust=.8,
vjust = .8, face="bold", size=20),
axis.title.y=theme_text(face="bold", size=16, angle=90, hjust=.3),
axis.title.x=theme_text(face="bold", size=16, vjust=-0.5),
axis.ticks=theme_segment(colour = "black", size=1),
panel.grid.minor=theme_blank() )

Hopefully, you have't already solved this. 


B

Brandon,

Thanks for your help. I actually woke up this morning and realized
that my problem was very simple. I didn't have the "#" in front of my
hex color codes. It worked after that. I have two more questions.

#1 - why is the extra legend appearing with the point size rather than
the point size being reflected in the legend?
#2 - how can I make the "LSKYesHatch" plot underneath the "LSKYes"
data so that LSKYes isn't overplotted?

Here is a reproducible example of the final working plot. It is a plot
of classifications from a single variable LDFA of fish. I wanted to
denote each classification with its own color AND symbol as well as
make clear which points have a known classification. Known origin
points have a higher luminance of the same color. There is also a red
group that I wanted to highlight because they are from a hatchery.

In this case all the classifications are correct, in other plots the
TrueClass column would plot the points in the column according to
their classification, but the ShapeClass column would plot it with
colors based on it's true classification. Misclassified points would
be easily visible in the wrong column since their shape and color
would be different. I also added a PlotOrder column to so columns go
from high y-values to low y-values. I'm sure there is a simpler way to
do this, this has been more about trial and error than anything.

That out of the way, you want to not overplot your Red and Cyan points. You can play with the height and width adjustments for geom_jitter().  Just add width= and/or height= to your jitter call. I couldn't get it completely non-overplotting. I would then perhaps try an alpha of the points. If that's not quite right... maybe a different kind of graph would be more appropriate? I have no idea what would be more appropriate though, I'm not a statistician. 

If you want to integrate legends you need to make sure they all have the same name, breaks and such. You need to add scale_size_manual().
